title: Food Tests
body_markdown:
A student was curious about the nutrients present in three samples of food, A, B and C. 
(a) The student carried out an experiment on each sample of food. 
 Several drops of iodine solution were added to food sample A and a blue-black colour was observed.
 5cm² of copper sulfate solution and 5cm² of dilute sodium hydroxide were added to food sample B and a purple colour was observed. 
 5cm² of ethanol was added to food sample C and the contents were shaken. When several drops of water were then added it was observed that the solution remained clear. Use the observations made by the student during each experiment to complete Table 1.1. 
(b) The student then decided to test two of the solid food samples for the presence of reducing sugar.
(i) Describe how the student would test each sample of food for the presence of reducing sugar. 
(ii) Complete Table 1.2 by stating a conclusion for each observation.

title: Insects
body_markdown:
Damselflies are flying insects that live near water in areas of Lesotho. Adult damselflies lay their eggs on plants. The eggs hatch into nymphs that feed on small water animals. During the next two years each nymph grows into an adult damselfly.
 A student investigated the growth of one damselfly nymph during one year from January to December and measured its mass on the first day of each month. 
 The student's results are shown in Table 2.1. 
(a) Use the data in table 2.1 to plot a graph to show how the mass of the nymph changed with time.
(b)(i) State the two months during which the nymph showed the least increase in mass.
(ii) Suggest two reasons why the nymph showed the least increase in mass during these two months.
(iii) Use the graph you have drawn to predict the mass of the nymph on the 15th September. 
(c) Suggest three ways in which the investigation could be improved to give more reliable or more accurate information about how the damselfly nymph develops into an adult damselfly.
